title: Leading-lagging indicator structure
note: Macroeconomic indicators come in three classes: leading (consumer sentiment, building permits, term spread), coincident (industrial production, employment), and lagging (unemployment, CPI, prime rate). The temporal sequence in the data — leading → coincident → lagging — is what makes a regime transition a 'real' macro signal rather than noise.

title: Term-structure inversions
note: 10y-3m and 10y-2y inversions have preceded most US recessions in the post-1970 era with a 6–18 month lead. The signal isn't deterministic — modern policy regime changes (active QT/QE) may have shifted the relationship — but inversions remain a high-information input alongside leading-indicator dispersion.
